practiceQuestions.q: On which date was the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly appointed?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee was appointed on August 29, 1947, to prepare a draft of the new Indian Constitution. Dec 9, 1946 was the first meeting, Nov 26, 1949 was adoption, and Jan 26, 1950 was commencement.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was appointed as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was unanimously elected as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee at its first meeting on August 30, 1947.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the total number of members in the Drafting Committee, including the Chairman?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee consisted of seven members: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer, Dr. K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rao (replaced B.L. Mitter), and T.T. Krishnamachari (replaced D.P. Khaitan).

practiceQuestions.q: Who replaced B.L. Mitter as a member of the Drafting Committee due to his ill health?
practiceQuestions.sol: B.L. Mitter resigned from the Drafting Committee due to ill health, and N. Madhava Rao was appointed in his place. T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan after Khaitan's death in 1948.

practiceQuestions.q: Who died in 1948, leading to his replacement by T.T. Krishnamachari in the Drafting Committee?
practiceQuestions.sol: D.P. Khaitan passed away in 1948, and T.T. Krishnamachari was chosen to fill the vacancy on the Drafting Committee.

practiceQuestions.q: Who served as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly, preparing the initial draft on which the Drafting Committee worked?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sir B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly. He prepared the first draft of the Constitution, consisting of 243 articles and 13 schedules, which was then scrutinized and debated by the Drafting Committee.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the chief draftsman of the constitution in the Constituent Assembly who put the draft into clear legal language?
practiceQuestions.sol: S.N. Mukherjee was the chief draftsman of the constitution in the Constituent Assembly, known for his ability to put complex provisions into crisp legal language.

practiceQuestions.q: How many sessions did the Constituent Assembly hold in total for the making of the Constitution?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to frame the Constitution, holding 11 sessions spread over 165 days.

practiceQuestions.q: When was the first draft of the Indian Constitution, prepared by the Drafting Committee, published?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee published the first draft of the Constitution in February 1948. People of India were given 8 months to discuss the draft and propose amendments.

practiceQuestions.q: How many readings did the draft constitution undergo in the Constituent Assembly before being adopted?
practiceQuestions.sol: The draft constitution underwent three readings in the Constituent Assembly. The third reading started on November 14, 1949, and ended on November 26, 1949, when the Constitution was declared passed.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the Drafting Committee considered the most critical committee of the Constituent Assembly among all other committees?
opts: It had the highest number of members from the princely states.
Its core task was to formulate the actual operational text and legal framework of the new Constitution based on various committee reports.
It was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who was also the President of the Constituent Assembly.
It functioned independently of the Constituent Assembly without needing approval.
practiceQuestions.sol: While other committees dealt with specific domains (like Union Powers, Provincial Constitution, etc.), the Drafting Committee was tasked with synthesizing these inputs and preparing the definitive text of the Constitution, making its role supreme.

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the working method of the Drafting Committee: How did it primarily arrive at decisions on contentious clauses?
opts: Strict majority voting by secret ballot
Direct orders and dictates from the British Viceroy
General consensus through deep deliberation and debate among members
Veto power exercised exclusively by the Chairman, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee and the Constituent Assembly largely worked through democratic debate, mutual persuasion, and general consensus rather than hard polarization or majoritarian dictation.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the public feedback period following the publication of the first draft in February 1948?
opts: It was a mandatory procedure demanded by the British Parliament under the Indian Independence Act, 1947.
It allowed the Drafting Committee to gauge public opinion, critiques, and suggestions, leading to thousands of amendments and the publication of a revised draft.
It delayed the Constitution so that princely states could negotiate separate treaties.
It was meant for general elections to be held prior to finalization.
practiceQuestions.sol: The publication of the draft invited intense scrutiny from citizens, press, and leaders. It resulted in over 7,000 proposed amendments, out of which over 2,400 were seriously discussed and considered by the committee.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the initial draft prepared by B.N. Rau differ from the final working document produced by the Drafting Committee?
opts: B.N. Rau's draft was written entirely in Urdu, while the committee's draft was in English.
B.N. Rau's draft focused only on fundamental rights, whereas the committee added economic provisions.
B.N. Rau provided a foundational technical blueprint/skeleton, which the Drafting Committee expanded, modified, and refined into a comprehensive constitutional text.
B.N. Rau's draft rejected federalism altogether, while the committee inserted federalism.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sir B.N. Rau studied constitutions across the world and prepared a comprehensive initial blueprint. The Drafting Committee took this structural base, added policy refinements, debated provisions, and restructured it into the final draft.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's role in the Drafting Committee often described as that of a 'pilot' and 'navigator' of the Constitution?
opts: Because he single-handedly wrote every single article without consulting anyone.
Because he expertly steered the complex draft through grueling debates, answered criticisms with immense patience and legal acumen, and defended provisions in the Assembly.
Because he flew to London multiple times to get approval from the British Crown.
Because he was in charge of transport and communication provisions in the Constitution.
practiceQuestions.sol: Dr. Ambedkar played a monumental role in steering the debate, explaining clauses, countering objections, and ensuring unity. His closing speeches in the Assembly highlight his intellectual leadership.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the composition of the Drafting Committee reflect geographical, social, and political representation of India?
opts: It exclusively comprised members from North India belonging to a single political party.
It brought together legal stalwarts from diverse regions, linguistic backgrounds, and legal expertise, bridging North-South and ideological divides.
It was dominated by British bureaucrats appointed by the Governor-General.
It represented only the Princely States and ignored British India provinces.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 7 members of the Drafting Committee included legal luminaries from different parts of India (such as Alladi from Madras, Ambedkar from Bombay/Central, Saadulla from Assam, Munshi from Bombay, etc.), ensuring pan-Indian representation and top-tier legal intellect.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary structural challenge faced by the Drafting Committee when they began drafting in August 1947?
opts: Absence of any written model anywhere in the world
Integrating diverse committee reports, dealing with partition aftermath, accommodating princely states, and synthesizing conflicting political ideologies.
Enforcing Hindi as the compulsory national language before drafting started
Holding nationwide general elections to elect committee members
practiceQuestions.sol: The committee had to reconcile varied reports from the Union Powers Committee, Provincial Constitution Committee, Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, etc., against the backdrop of partition, communal violence, and integration challenges.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Drafting Committee manage the humongous task of scrutinizing amendments proposed by Assembly members?
opts: By rejecting all amendments outright without reading them
By delegating amendment scrutiny to sub-committees and conducting meticulous clause-by-clause evaluation during intensive sittings.
By forwarding all amendments to the Privy Council in London for voting
By restricting amendments to only those proposed by the Prime Minister
practiceQuestions.sol: The committee sat continuously for months, examining thousands of amendments clause-by-clause, modifying language, and defending alterations in the Constituent Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: In what way did the Drafting Committee influence India's transition from colonial rule to a sovereign democratic republic?
opts: By retaining the Government of India Act 1935 as the permanent constitution without changes
By drafting a transformative constitution embodying universal adult franchise, fundamental rights, federalism, and social justice, dismantling colonial structures.
By establishing a presidential system modelled strictly on the United States
By declaring India a dominion permanently under British protection
practiceQuestions.sol: The Drafting Committee crafted a visionary document that broke away from colonial authoritarianism, anchoring India in democratic constitutionalism, social revolution, and republicanism.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Drafting Committee's work often cited as a masterclass in comparative constitutional engineering?
opts: Because they copied the US Constitution word-for-word without alterations.
Because they ingeniously cherry-picked and adapted best practices from multiple global constitutions while tailoring them to India's unique socioeconomic realities.
Because they rejected all foreign influences and relied solely on ancient Vedic texts.
Because they completed the entire constitution in a single afternoon.
practiceQuestions.sol: The committee drew from British parliamentary democracy, US fundamental rights, Irish DPSP, Canadian federalism, etc., blending them seamlessly into a cohesive constitutional framework tailored for India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Drafting Committee:
1. It was set up on August 29, 1947, to prepare a draft of the new Constitution.
2. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was appointed as its Chairman.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Drafting Committee was indeed established on August 29, 1947, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar served as its Chairman.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Drafting Committee:
1. It had a total of nine members including the Chairman.
2. Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar were among its members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Drafting Committee had 7 members, not 9. Statement 2 is correct as Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar were prominent members of the 7-member committee.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the personnel changes in the Drafting Committee:
1. B.L. Mitter resigned due to ill health and was replaced by N. Madhava Rao.
2. D.P. Khaitan died in 1948 and was replaced by T.T. Krishnamachari.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are factually correct. B.L. Mitter stepped down due to illness (replaced by N. Madhava Rao), and D.P. Khaitan passed away in 1948 (replaced by T.T. Krishnamachari).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the timeline and enactment of the Constitution:
1. The Drafting Committee published its first draft of the Constitution in February 1948.
2. The Constitution was adopted and enacted on November 26, 1949.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The first draft was out in Feb 1948, allowing 8 months for public feedback, and the Constitution was adopted on Nov 26, 1949.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the drafting process and key officials:
1. Sir B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor who prepared the initial draft of the Constitution.
2. S.N. Mukherjee served as the chief draftsman of the constitution in the Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. B.N. Rau prepared the initial blueprint, and S.N. Mukherjee put provisions into legal phrasing as the chief draftsman.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the discussions on the draft Constitution:
1. The draft constitution was subjected to three readings in the Constituent Assembly.
2. The entire process of drafting and enacting the Constitution took exactly 5 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (3 readings took place). Statement 2 is incorrect because the Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days, not 5 years.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the role of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar:
1. He was elected as a member of the Constituent Assembly from Bengal before partition.
2. After partition, he re-entered the Constituent Assembly from the Bombay province.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Dr. Ambedkar was initially elected from the Jessore-Khulna region of Bengal. When that area went to East Pakistan, his seat became vacant, and he was subsequently re-elected from Bombay.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functioning and outputs of the Drafting Committee:
1. The committee only reviewed articles related to fundamental rights and ignored administrative provisions.
2. It considered thousands of amendments submitted by public and Assembly members during its sittings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the committee reviewed the entire constitutional text covering legislative, executive, judicial, federal, and emergency provisions, not just fundamental rights. Statement 2 is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the passage of the Constitution:
1. The third reading of the draft constitution concluded on November 26, 1949.
2. On the same day, the Constituent Assembly adopted, enacted, and gave to themselves the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The third reading ended on Nov 26, 1949, with a motion passed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar ('The Constitution as settled by the Assembly be passed'), leading to its formal adoption.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historical context of the Drafting Committee:
1. It functioned under continuous external pressure from the British colonial administration which dictated amendments.
2. Its members represented a blend of eminent jurists, administrators, and political leaders of independent India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constituent Assembly and its committees functioned as a sovereign body under the Indian Independence Act 1947, free from British dictation. Statement 2 is correct.
